articleTitle: Investigation of the Effect of Different Shading Scale on the Operating of Photovoltaic Modules Using Numerical Simulations
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The photovoltaic (PV) module is the basic building block of each photovoltaic system. Output power of the PV module and the produced energy strongly depends on the operating conditions. The operating temperature of the device, ambient temperature, solar radiation intensity, humidity, and dustiness can be considered as the most important factors. A significant decrease of delivered power occurs in the case of partial or complete shading of PV module, which comes e.g. from clouds, surrounding buildings, pillars, snow or e.g. from various impurities (bird droppings). This shading brings, in addition to power loss, an associated problem of existence two (or more) power maxima in the P-V curve. Existence of "two knees" on the I-V characteristic can negatively affect the operation of the associated electronics (MPP tracker). No less important problem related to power losses is creation of the hotspots (places of excessive local heating). Shaded part of the module behaves like an electric load and converts electric energy into joule heat. Hotspot affects safety (fire, destruction of equipment) and reliability of electricity supply from PV device. Comprehensively analysis of the negative consequences of the different degree of shading of the PV module parts, as well as the role of bypass diodes following the reliability in power engineering is very useful. Practical experiments on created experimental PV module were confronted with the simulations in MATLAB. Presentation of simulation and results useful for practice are main aim of this paper.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Improving COP of Peltier Cells Operating as a Heat Pump
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Peltier cell (hereinafter PC) has undergone technological development since it’s discovery by Joan C. Peltier in 1834, and from the point of view of theoretical physics they can be considered completely explored. They are commonly used for low-power cooling (for example car refrigerators) and for temperature control (controlled electronics cooling), ie mostly in low-power applications from the point of view of the power industry. We are currently experiencing enormous pressure to save energy and use waste heat, so the question arises as to whether it would not be possible to dust off the idea of “energy” use of PC.

articleTitle: Some Aspects of Building Integrated Photovoltaics Operation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Building Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) is an option which offers renewable energy production and environmental friendly technology in the situation of actually increasing energy demand and threatening climate changes. When building materials are replaced by BIPV, new challenges to be solved appear. We discuss various aspects which are specific in BIPV in comparison with standard ground installed photovoltaics. Results obtained by simulation and experimental measurements related to the BIPV operation are also presented.

articleTitle: Improving the Operation of Power System Control During Disturbances Using FACTS Controllers
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The rapidly evolving FACTS systems, especially thanks to the more technically majestic power semiconductor devices, are opening a new era in their more frequent and immediate implementations into the power system. Presented research with simulation in the program matlab Simulink. Mathematical control types SVC, STATCOM, SSSC and UPFC are compiled together with controllers for PSS and AVR generators. The main goal is to compare the operation with the use of FACTS controllers and without them for short circuits. On a simple network model (from production to consumption), selected FACTS devices are inserted into the diagrams. Their impact on function and the ability to improve quality, safety, reliability and toughness is summarized in the conclusion.

articleTitle: Cost Assessment of Battery Hybrid Energy Storage System for Full-Electric Marine Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the optimal sizing and cost assessment of onboard battery hybrid energy storage system (HESS) for full-electric marine applications. In this regard, a harbor tug is selected as the use case and the cost of different full-active HESS topologies is compared against a baseline topology with a single type battery. The NMC and LTO battery chemistries are selected as the high-energy (HE) and high-power (HP) battery technologies in this work. The baseline and HESS battery topologies are sized for a design life of10 years considering the battery aging. The results show that by a parallel full-active HESS topology, the battery pack cost can be reduced around 28% and 14% compared to a monotype battery topology with LTO and NMC cells, respectively. The results of this study imply that hybridization could be a promising solution to reduce the cost of large batteries within the maritime sector.

articleTitle: Simplified Dynamic Model for Continental Europe Synchronous Area Separation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with frequency stability simulations for large disturbances such as synchronous area separation. It shows the process of preparation and validation of the simplified dynamic model for Continental Europe separation from January, 8, 2021, in which the single machine equivalent was used for modelling of power system dynamics. The model is suitable for examination of dynamic behavior of both islands which were created after the separation.

articleTitle: Application of Capacitor to Distribution System for Minimization of Power Looses
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Generating reactive power in a power plant and delivering the load over long distances is not economically acceptable, but this reactive power is simply provided by capacitors or excited motors in the load centers. The distribution system usually has two main problems, high power loss and poor voltage profile. One of the reasons for low power factor losses is that if the power factor is low, the current will increase and as a result there will be additional losses of active power in all elements of the energy system. One way to minimize technical losses and improve the voltage profile is the optimal location or installation of capacitor banks in the distribution system. This paper describes the static and dynamic effects of placing capacitor banks on busbars of a 20 kV system in distribution systems using measurements and tests performed before and after the installation of capacitor banks 3.42 MVAr and capacitor banks 2.16 MVAr systems. Load analysis is performed to predict the magnitude of the supply current, power factor, voltage levels and total losses in the system branches. The size of the capacitor batteries is also designed to maintain an acceptable power factor.

articleTitle: Energy Dependency : Worldwide Energy Situation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper focuses on current energy situation with respect to the last days changes. Energy dependency of the European Union is described, and the last statistics are presented. Energy situation in Slovakia is shown in detail. Finally, the possible scenarios and plans how to reduce energy dependency of the European Union are discussed.

articleTitle: Power Grid and Data Network Simulator
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper is focused on the research of a complex model including the simulation of interconnected power and data infrastructure. Given the absence of a similar solution, the paper is focused on the verification of the impact of power system outages on individual elements of a data network or critical infrastructure. These outputs will then be used for further development of the described simulator.

articleTitle: Marine Solution for PEM Fuel Cells in AC or DC Grid
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells are a promising source of energy in shipping, due to its zero carbon and zero pollution operation. This article is focused on the use of PEM fuel cells, which are currently the most common in maritime sector. The often use of PEM fuel cells is also because of international and regional regulations, which require significant reduction of emissions. Operation of PEM fuel cells onboard vessel brings potential risk, however when safety countermeasures are ensured PEM fuel cells are safe to use as well as any other power sources. Vessels are typically equipped with either AC grid or DC grid. Both has different benefits, which are useful in certain applications. Due to that, PEM fuel cells must be able to be integrated into AC and DC grid. Individual examples of integration and their requirements are described in this article.

articleTitle: Ship to Shore Connection
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article focuses on the ship’s electrical connection to the port, which appears to be an important technological element that will reduce air pollution in ports. Ports therefore install facilities that allow mooring ships to connect to the port distribution network. By 2025, this will be mandatory for all ports in Europe. That is why Shore Connection technology is experiencing a huge boom. All this means that in the future all ships staying in the port will have to be able to connect to the port and then power all their electrical appliances from the onshore distribution network. The ships will have to shut down their generators as soon as possible so that they no longer burn fossil fuels, which cause significant air pollution. Because ships near the port have to burn more expensive, greener fuels, it is often economically advantageous for them to connect to port distribution network. It is often cheaper for ships to buy electricity from the grid than to produce it with their own generators. Shore Connection must therefore be considered in the production of new ships, but this function is also being added on a large scale to already manufactured ships. This article discusses the most important devices that must be newly installed to connect to the port. The procedure for connecting a ship to a port is explained using an example of a Shore Connection solution supplied by ABB.

articleTitle: Defects of Photovoltaic Panels
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article briefly summarizes the issue of photovoltaic panels from the point of their failure rate and the occurrence of degradation processes. The individual chapters outline the methods of diagnostics of photovoltaic panel defects and their possible solutions.

articleTitle: Stochastic Concept for Modeling Distributed Energy Resources in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Distributed energy resources have become a stable and rapidly growing part of power systems. DER character and properties depend significantly on the type used technology and application. Their common feature is the probabilistic nature of their behavior and parameters. Penetration of DER into classical power systems raises the question of power quality and operational safety. This paper presents a general method to implement any DER into a custom power system and calculate the probabilities of possible impacts. The proposed method is based on the combination of deterministic, probabilistic, unknown parameters and information about investigating power system and future scenarios of DER penetration. The Paper also presents a case scenario where penetration of PV system into low voltage network is investigated. The last part shows the complex result of probabilistic power flow calculations. Presented methods have been used for practical applications to determine hosting capacity for PV systems in rural and urban areas of the Slovak republic.

articleTitle: Utilization of Battery Storage System in the Production of Electricity from a Photovoltaic Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the case of cooperation of energy storage system with renewable sources and distribution network. The photovoltaic power plant was considered in the case study as a renewable energy source. Energy storage system was considered as a general energy system that can be adapted to the needs of the electrical network and therefore it could be considered as a prosumer. Simulink was chosen as the simulation tool, which provided obtaining sufficiently accurate results for the considered 48-hour interval. The results were confronted at the end of paper.

articleTitle: Possibilities of Software Goniophotometer usage for LED Luminaires Luminous Intensity Distribution Curves Modelling – Case Study
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article deals with the modelling of the required luminous intensity distribution curve (LIDC) using software for lighting systems designing. Theoretical part of article, partially describes the software, its calculation and modelling in connection with implemented software goniophotometer. The practical part (case study) is focused on LIDCs modelling. For this example, there were prepared LIDCs which fit the lighting systems in city parks. It means that LIDCs will illuminated large areas from small heights and by relatively small luminous flux. This section will explain and show in details how to create such a LIDC and export it to the required file (LDT), thus creating a new luminaire with the required LIDC. Subsequently, a model space (city park) will be created in the software. This allows to test the individual newly created luminaires and compared with respect to needed parameters.

articleTitle: Influence of Tension Insulators and Bundle Conductors on Sag of Conductors in Substations
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Influence of tensile insulators on conductor tensile force is an issue that is still overlooked in detail today. The motivation of this article is to introduce the correct and analytic computational approach, which includes the bundle conductors in symmetrical spans. Bundle conductors are not mentioned in the basic mechanical tension formulas, and therefore some self-made modifications in this manner were not always correctly carried out. Our inclusion of bundled conductors into the state equation of the short span is verified through numerical computations (FEM) in PLS-CADD software. The results are applicable in the substation design, where such short spans with bundled conductors occurs the most. Furthermore, an analysis was carried out to show the line between the long and short span definition.

articleTitle: Exploitation experience in partial discharge diagnostics of power transformers
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper presents exploitation experience in partial discharge (PD) diagnostics of power transformers, with particular consideration of practical aspects and potential limitation of the contemporary measuring techniques. The objective of this study is to indicate typical problems related to PD diagnostics of power transformers and to propose practical solutions based on simultaneous application of several PD measuring methods. Three case studies based on real life scenarios are used to illustrate practical aspects and potential limitation of the contemporary PD diagnostics. Each scenario addresses a different PD issue, and different measurement results achieved using electrical, UHF and acoustic emission (AE) methods. Presented results extend the state-of-art through the detailed analysis of presented exploitation case studies. Thus, it may be potentially used for optimization of the maintenance process and improvements of PD diagnostics regarding power transformers.

articleTitle: An Efficient Technique to Reduce Total Harmonics Distortion of Single-Phase Voltage Source Inverter Output Current
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Harmonics are generally classified as the most well-known problem in the distribution system. Nowadays also linked to inverter-based power generating units. In this paper an effective technique to reduce total harmonic distortion in output voltage and current of a single-phase voltage source DC/AC Inverter is proposed and evaluated by means of simulations. Based on using passive filters, and PWM open loop and closed loop control, the inverter is designed to achieve the output waveform as close as possible to the sinusoidal wave. The proposed inverter filter and control design main characteristic is the ability to consider the presence of harmonics and make them less than 5 %. The performance of this approach in the inverter development has been proven in the PSIM environment.

Author Keywords: Single phase voltage source inverter VSI

articleTitle: Virtualization Platform for Urban Infrastructure
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Current open-source solutions do not include the possibility of simultaneous simulation of a data network and a power grid. The purpose of this paper is to describe the design of a simulation platform that will provide this type of simulation. The created virtualization platform that consists of several open-source tools is described in detail. The paper further deals with the description of data network virtualization and interconnection with power grid simulation. The architecture described aims to solve the missing solution of the simulation of data network and power grid interconnection.

articleTitle: Voltage Stability of Power System of the Slovak Republic: Influence of Transformers with AVR
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article deals with voltage stability of the power system (PS) and its assessment based on PV curves. We introduce an analysis of the influence of transformers with automatic voltage regulator (AVR) on the shape of PV curves and magnitude of voltage on the side of transmission system (TS) and distribution system (DS). The article was carried out in cooperation with the Slovak TSO – Slovenská elektrizačná prenosová sústava, a.s.

articleTitle: Analysis and Verification of Operating Characteristics of Hybrid Inverter with External Power Meter
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the non-standard behavior of a hybrid inverter equipped with external measurement, which was observed during one of the many tests performed in the ResLab laboratory at Brno University of Technology. It focuses on the inverter control processes which intend to maintain a power flow balance within the hybrid system consisting of photovoltaic source, battery storage and load. The paper contains a theoretical background, a description of the hybrid system configuration together with the laboratory equipment used for the test purposes, a simulated scenario, measurements results and its evaluation. The results show that the inverter does not fulfill its function in certain situations and its operation may even have a negative impact on the distribution grid at the point of common coupling.

articleTitle: Forecasting of Smart Meters Energy Consumption for Data Analytics and Grid Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Using data from smart meters for billing issue is an obvious application of Smart Metering. But focusing on smart metering data analytics for grid monitoring and automation is missing. The paper focuses on possibilities of using data from smart meters for data analytics and gridmonitoring (Smart Metering application beyond billing data). The paper deals with two use cases for which the prediction and forecasting of energy consumption is crucial. The first use case is the estimated consumption and energy values for grid monitoring (possibility to forecast energy values for predicted potential events) and the second use case is to compare the consumption of all Smart Meters in the particular location with the measurement of total consumption in the substation (sum of all consumptions - black consumption identification or protection of energy grid during various disturbances). Counting data from non-communicating electricity meters is necessary for grid monitoring and ability to measure all electrical values in synchronized power system measurements.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of Photovoltaic Cell Defects and Their Impact on Electricity Generation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Renewable sources are currently a widely used source of electricity. They are also supported within the European Union. Defects in photovoltaic panels often occur during the implementation and operation of photovoltaic panels. Not all defects can be seen. In practice, it happens that no attention is paid to defects that occur during the operation of the photovoltaic power plant. These defects cause a decrease in electricity production, which reduces the efficiency of this renewable source. This paper describes defects that occur during the implementation and operation of a photovoltaic panel. Based on the performed simulations, the authors describe how defects affect the performance of the photovoltaic panel. Simulations were focused on changing parallel and serial resistance in the simulation model. Results describe the effect changing of serial and parallel resistance to production of electricity from the photovoltaic panels. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Computer Methods of Fault Study in Power Systems Consider the Effect of Load
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In fault studies, many researchers ignore the effect of load to the fault current. This paper presents a solution and develop a tool for analyzing the fault in power system with load so-called “Power System Fault Analysis (PSFA)”. The accuracy and effectiveness of this tool are compared with the simulation results from the Power World software. From the obtained results, the effect of load to the fault current in power system will be discussed.

articleTitle: Time Courses of Luminance on a Road Illuminated by an Adaptive Lighting System
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article describes the basic characteristics of adaptive or biodynamic lighting systems and their effects on the human body and the artificial luminance on the night sky. In the second part, it describes the luminance measurements made on a road illuminated by such a lighting system from the manufacturer Tungsram, with emphasis on the description of changes of luminance with respect to time. The measurements were taken with a luminance analyzer and the results show a smooth decline of luminance of the road – from the 100 % in the beginning to approx. 77,5 % during the first phase and from those 77,5 % to approximately 40,5 % during the second phase of the switching.

articleTitle: Evaluation of voltage dip performance of 110 kV networks in the context of voltage quality regulation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In comparison with continuity of supply, voltage dips are regulated only in a few European countries. Before setting limits of voltage dips for regulatory purposes, a detailed analysis of historical records has to be carried out and various aspects of voltage event counting have to be considered. The paper summarizes the results of long-term voltage dip monitoring in the 110 kV system. Statistics of voltage dip performance at the site and system-level concerning the severity of dips are completed by the historical trend of system indices. Counting of dips concerning their impact on customers is also discussed.

articleTitle: Combined simulation of grid and power plant operation with a pairing to a real MicroGrid
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper introduces the data pairing and operational coupling of a power plant (PP) simulator, a grid simulator with focus on a transmission grid and a real microgrid. The concept of the interaction of the three systems for research, education and training in the current context of the energy transition and the nuclear as well as the coal phase-out in Germany is described.

articleTitle: Implementation of distributed control system for controlling energy processes
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article focuses on the possibilities of controlling energy processes using a distributed control system 800xA from the company ABB. The principle is explained on the example of controlling the pyrolysis unit. First, the article discusses the design of new hardware needed to control the pyrolysis process. The second chapter deals with the creation of a control application in the Control Builder environment, where the solution of optimal heating is given, considering the large thermal inertia of heating using resistance spirals. The third chapter describes the possibilities of creating a graphical control display for control from a PC in the Engineering Workplace environment. The fifth chapter deals with the Panel Builder software, in which it is possible to create the settings of the built-in touch panel.

articleTitle: Drift from cooling towers as an important emission source, its measurement and reduction
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Safe and effective operation of any powerplant requires efficient control of any emission among others, which could have impact on ambient environment. CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>, dust and others are well recognized pollutants, which emissions are strictly controlled. However, there are other emissions, which are not on the radar yet. There is no common legislation in the EU for these emissions. One of the overlooked sources of emissions is drift.Every powerplant requires cooling. Major part of them uses significant number of cooling towers to cool down the mixture of hot water and steam back to water in the condensers so that it can be used again in the whole thermal cycle. Any cooling tower releases heat into the environment, it is its function, but with the heat it releases significant amount of water. Major quantity is released due to the evaporation, which is the wet cooling principle. But there is also not minor (especially on big cooling towers) part in a form of drift. The water loss due to its evaporation could not be reduced (if only wet cooling is used) while the drift could be significantly lowered. This paper presents drift measurement principals and introduces new method, which is being developed for simpler, faster and more economical drift determination.

articleTitle: Assessment of Typical Shutdowns in CHP Plant
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper is focused on assessment of typical operational constraints at combined heat and power plant in Pilsen. The plant has been chosen because there have been operated various production technologies. All the technologies have been assessed by key availability parameters e.g., number of shutdowns and shutdown time. Obtained availability parameters for the technologies and significant causes of shutdowns have been assessed. Moreover, the paper presents the solutions to improve the current state at the plant in Pilsen.

articleTitle: Biogas and Biomethane from Animal Waste for Electricity Production
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The biogas or biomethane production process is becoming a great potential for the development of Polish agriculture and gives many benefits the environment i.e a reduction of methane emissions to the atmosphere or limitation of landfills. In the paper the current situation and perspective for the development of agricultural biogas plants in Poland is presented. Additionally, an analysis of the biogas and biomethane production potential from animal manure in Poland and Opolskie voivodship was presented. The calculation showed that both for the country and the voivodship the largest potential for electricity production was found for cattle manure (about 4 mln MWh) and cow manure (about 2 mln MWh).

articleTitle: Co-simulating fault events in the on- and off-site electrical system of a nuclear power plant
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Continuous search for safety enhancements, reported events from the past and changes in the power system motivate studies on the impact of power systems in the safety of operations of nuclear power plants (NPP). The on- and off-site systems of an NPP have interactions with each other, but these are usually simulated with separate tools and with varying levels of detail. This paper builds on previous work in developing a co-simulation platform that connects the simulation of the thermomechanical and automation systems of an NPP with the simulation of the related electrical power systems, composed of the on-site grid and the off-site grid (transmission system). This co-simulation platform enables the integration of largescale NPP models and performance of fault-based simulations to evaluate the impacts of selected grid fault scenarios on NPP operations. This paper presents an overview of the simulation models, describes the tested fault scenarios that affect both on- and off-site electrical grids, and offers a comparison between simulation results obtained with the co-simulation platform and simulations comprising only the electrical systems, which treat the NPP as a black-box. The presented results show the disturbance response at various system levels, allow comparison with alarms and protection function limits and assess where the co-simulation approach may be of benefit.

articleTitle: Development of Hardening Machine and Intelligent Control
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article focuses on introducing the developed hardening machine based on induction heating. This machine differs significantly from conventional solutions mainly due to its extensive measuring system, which gives us a complete overview of what is happening during the process. Furthermore, the developed control system using PLC is described. This paper also mentions the design of own control of the frequency converter using microcontrollers.

articleTitle: Comparison of connected compensation unit for induction machine operation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with research in the field of power factor compensation for induction motors. The main goal was to verify the effect of the compensation unit connected to the induction machine during start-up and no-load state. The connected compensation unit consists of either power capacitors or a combination of power capacitors and detuned reactors. Individual measurements were made on an induction motor with a nominal power output of 4 kW. As part of the measurement, the connected compensation stages for total harmonic distortion were also verified. In the final part there is a comparison of individual variants and recommendations for further research in the subject area.

articleTitle: Calculation of the three-core cable operating capacitance
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Operating capacitance is one of the basic parameters of medium voltage cables. This value varies based on the cable type and is usually defined by the manufacturer. Presented paper deals with the calculation of the operating capacitance of the three-core belted cable using analytical relations, as well as using the programs EMTP-ATP and COMSOL. The problem of the analytical method in determining the mutual potential coefficients and the problems of capacitance determination by the software COMSOL have been described. This paper compares the results of the relationships derived by its authors and the results of the relationships obtained from the available literature.

articleTitle: Intelligent solutions in the energy sector as climate and environment protection factors
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Subject and purpose of the dissertation includes presentation of authorial solutions having both technical and organizational character and regarding energy sector in the ecological aspect. Materials and methods incorporates a compendium of knowledge on intelligent solutions for the energy sector pertaining to the major fields of activity that may raise the efficiency of its operation significantly. On the basis of research concluded and both technical and econometric analyses carried out, it has been indicated that the implementation of authorial solution is justified as it increases the possibility of influencing the ecological aspects of the energy sector in the upcoming future. It is essential to conduct further research in this area to examine dynamic changes and eliminate the negative impact of the energy sector on environment.

articleTitle: Determination of the Optimal Reference Signal Frequency in the Task of Power Spectrum Pattern Classification
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article describes the results of an experiment in which a reference signal with its subsequent processing is used to obtain information on the degree of cable insulation degradation. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network is used for signal classification. The reference signal was tested with two methods of insulation degradation, thermal and electrical. The signal was preprocessed to obtain its power spectrum density. After that the obtained result was sent to the input of the neural network. Based on the learning and validation curves and the confusion classification matrices, the optimal frequencies of the reference signal were found.

articleTitle: Role of Simulation of Power Output in the Design of Small-scale Hydro Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Article focuses on importance of time power-output simulation performed in Matlab in order to identify real hydroelectric potential in selected locations of river flows in the Czech Republic. The difference of simulation and the usual total generated power in a time-period might play a significant role in decision making during realization of a small-scale hydro power plant. The greatest difference is the view on generation from the time perspective throughout the year which can show the critical periods in the year when the generation is low or when it’s maximal. This simulation approach also shows the difference between annual generated electricity using average flows and the actual hourly flows. In the modern plant design real data time simulation should play nowadays a stadard role.

articleTitle: Preparation and Analysis of a Thin Composite Membrane for Electroacoustic Applications
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In this paper, elastic soft composite silicone has been used to produce membrane for an electroacoustic device. 80 μm iron powder in a silicone matrix was used in the spin coating process. Membranes have been created with different thicknesses and different iron contents. The properties of the composite microstructure were investigated using a scanning electron microscope. A measurement system for the acoustic power of the system was built. A large influence of membrane thickness on the acoustic response has been demonstrated. The influence of production parameters on the distribution of iron grains was shown and related to the acoustic response. The collections between the membrane structure are shown. The presented electroacoustic device can be used as a low-power loudspeaker.

articleTitle: Utilization of FEM Model for Validation of Induction Coil Sensor in Diagnosis of Rotor Defects
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with the design of a simple and relatively reliable method for offline diagnostics of asynchronous motor rotors shortly after casting. Numerical simulation is used for the basic design of the overall arrangement of the rotor to be measured, the sensors and the measurement system as a whole. Using transient electromagnetic analysis, a set of output signals from the sensor is searched for that clearly identifies a possible rotor fault, such as a partially or fully broken bar.. FFT analysis, which is part of the simulation software, is used for the overall processing of the simulated values. The solution results are then compared and validated using measurements on the real rotor with the sensors constructed according to the previous simulations.

articleTitle: Use of active power filter to reduce flicker caused by electric arc furnace operation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Effectiveness of using a parallel active power filter to compensate for the flicker of an electric arc furnace, and mitigate the reactive power consumption and terminal voltage variation in the grid is presented and evaluated in the contribution. The model of a power system with the electric arc furnace and parallel active power filter in the frequency domain has been developed. The selected results of simulation in the frequency domain using the data collected from the 60 t EAF are presented and evaluated.

articleTitle: Analysis Backup Battery for Photovoltaic Power Plants Using the MCA Method
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This article describes the use of multi-criteria analysis when choosing a backup battery for the accumulation of produced electricity by a renewable source - a photovoltaic power plant. The first part defines the individual accumulators and their properties. A total of six battery selection options, six criteria for evaluating the characteristics and the corresponding weight selection of these criteria are described. Three methods of calculating MCA were selected for evaluation and their results were compared.

articleTitle: Influence of Short Segments with Different Thermal Conductivity on Operating Temperature of Cable Routes
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The ampacity (current carrying capacity) of cable routes is an important parameter for assessment the economical and safe supply of electricity. The cables often routed through short segments such as walls, ceilings, fire barriers etc., which have different thermal conductivity than environment of the other parts of cable route. Although, the length of short segments can be negligible in comparison to the entire length of the cable route, their impact on ampacity of the cable route can play a significant role. Experimentally measured results of temperature of a low voltage cable used in building installations passes through wall from wood, aerated concrete block and mineral wool at different current loads are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Electromobility Charging Behavior Modeling Using Polynomial Regression Approach
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: As is electromobility is still expanding, its effects on the power grid need to be expected and be prepared for. This paper is analyzing the possibilities of creating a very simple probabilistic model while keeping the outputs still accurate enough for most of the applications in power engineering. The simplicity and flexibility of this model are proposed by using the polynomial regression on the initial probability density functions and weighted random choices variables. These approximations are then defined in all the time frames during the simulation, which makes also the time step easily variable. The proper means of finding the polynomial regression functions are introduced, as well as the usage in the complete probabilistic model algorithm. Verification of the proposed model is carried out using open data. Applications and further extensions of the model are discussed.

articleTitle: Personal Safety for Persons in Vicinity of MV-Cables During Earth Faults
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The potential differences in the immediate vicinity of an earth fault location of 20 kV and 30 kV cables in earth fault current-limited grids (ohmic or resonant) are analyzed with regard to personal safety for general public, which might be barefoot. Not only occurring step voltages are assessed but also accessible touch voltages on the surface for persons in push-up-position. Two main fault scenarios are in the focus. The first scenario is a cable earth fault, where some part of the fault current flows through the damaged insulation into earth and causes a rise of surface potential in the vicinity, which can lead to step or touch voltages. In the second scenario the transferred potential via accompanying earth electrode in the case of earth faults in the nearby ring main unit (RMU) or cable termination tower is analyzed.Based on the investigations carried out, in the case of internal faults cables in medium voltage grids (resonant or current-limited) in practical cases, no danger to persons is to be expected with regard to impermissible body currents or potential differences (touch voltages, step voltages). Likewise, it can be assumed in the typical networks and situations, that there is no danger to persons due to transferred potential with the accompanying earth electrodes, especially if the earth potential rise (EPR) of the connected earthing system is less than four times the permissible touch voltage.

articleTitle: Distribution of relaxation times during accelerated thermal aging of insulating nanofluids
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper deals with the dynamics of the distribution of relaxation times in the investigated fluids with two different types of dispersed nanoparticles during accelerated thermal aging. The introduction reflects an overview of the use of progressive nanofluids, followed by an explanation of production methodology. The results are analyzed by frequency-dependent dielectric spectroscopy in the frequency band and using the ColeCole principle to determine the degree of distribution of relaxation times. The analysis contains an electrophysical description of captured relaxation processes with a specific origin, which causes a dielectric response to the AC electric field.

articleTitle: Dispatch Reactive Power Sharing Concept for Power Generating Plants in Medium Voltage Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the recent years, distributed generation modules are penetrating into the low voltage and medium voltage distribution system. In medium voltage systems, however, the more emphasis is on the coordination of voltage control due to the impact to the low voltage systems, and reactive power over distribution transformer due to the impact to high voltage systems. Throughout the paper, the mechanisms of the coordination are described in detail and examples of reactive power dispatch algorithms reveal the potential of reactive power delivery to high voltage system as a consequence of the reactive power sharing between individual generating modules.

articleTitle: A Review of the Use of Phasor Measurement Units in Power System State Estimation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Today’s power systems are facing great challenges because of increasing expansions, variable loads and renewable energy sources on the distribution systems, and growing demand to connect the networks together. As a result, estimation of the power system state is becoming an important task in modern power systems due to the increase of its complexity. Continuous development in synchrophasor measurement technology and communication systems enhances and encourages researchers and electric utilities to employ this technology to improve the performance of power system operation, control, protection, and state estimation (SE). A review of the methods used for power system state estimation is presented in this paper. This paper essentially aims to focus on the applications of Phasor Measurement Units for Power System SE. Issues of conventional state estimation process based on wide-area monitoring (excluding Phasor Measurement Units) and Supervisory Control And Data Acquisition (SCADA) system have been highlighted. In addition, the paper investigates studies from the literature to show the possibilities and advantages brought by the synchrophasor measurement technology for Power System State Estimation.

articleTitle: Overview on Synchrophasors Technology and Trend of their Application in Electrical Network Protection
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Due to the complexity and increasing challenges faced in today’s power system because of the increasing demand in electrical energy, integration of renewable energies and other distributed energy resources, highly responsive and more reliable tools granting outstanding system observability are required. However, the recent advances in control, sensing, computation, and satellite communication technologies, the use of the global positioning system (GPS) providing users with positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) services, as well as the development of time-stamped measurement technology (SMT), are enormously contributing in making the real-time system monitoring possible. In addition, the recently developed phasor measurement units (PMU) which can provide 30 to 120 timetagged measurements per second increases the proper system observability. This work explores and reviews the synchrophasor technology and the trend of its applications in power system protection and their contribution in bridging the existing gap in protection, control, and monitoring of the Power system.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of Induction Heating Process Control
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Modern induction heating technology (IHT) aims to regulate the heat generation inside the billet to obtain the target temperature at the desired location and time. This study presents a mathematical and numerical model that describes what occurs on the surface of the workpiece during induction heating (IH), simulating the events on the surface and the temperature change inside the workpiece. The analysis used different heating control techniques to achieve the target temperature using the COMSOL Multiphysics 6.0 software. I have developed three different algorithms to analyze the temperature distribution from the surface to the core: explicit and implicit event control algorithms and discrete frequency control aligned to the coil current. This article also covered the two vital electromagnetic properties, electrical conductivity and magnetic permeability, which significantly impact the performance of the IH system and its efficiency.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Performance of Concentrated Monocrystalline Silicon Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Cell temperature is a critical factor that is frequently neglected when the performance of solar cells is estimated. Its effect is especially crucial in high-illumination, high-temperature circumstances in various terrestrial hybrid systems. This study shows how the electric energy generation of a mono-crystalline silicon solar cell varies with light concentration level if the thermal dissipation of the module is considered. This paper introduced a literature method of solar cell parameters extraction and model verification. The effects of solar insolation G and cell temperature T are evaluated. In this work, an analysis has been carried out to evaluate the electrical and thermal performance of the CPV model. It assesses temperature-dependent solar cell performance under concentrated illumination. The results indicate that the efficiency of full spectrum concentrated Si PV cells increases with concentration, but at a certain point the negative effects of the temperature rise of the PV-cell will suppress positive effects of light concentration and the efficiency starts to decrease again. The PV cell efficiency of concentrated visible light spectrum is higher than the efficiency of full spectrum illumination at the same concentration level due to its lower temperature. The proposed model describes an easy method to estimate the optimal concentration level for a solar cell based on the cell’s datasheet and the parameters of the applied heat sink.

articleTitle: Voltage Based Phase Identification Method, Robustness and Validation
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: One of the problems of full-scale utilization of per phase measured smart meter data is the uncertainty whether phase labeling between different metering locations belongs to the same actual phase. This uncertainty poses a risk that the measured data might be misinterpreted. This problem has been addressed by introducing many different phase identification methods which one of these, voltage based, is investigated in this paper. The function of this method was tested on a real deployed measurement that should have represented scenario of smart meter measurements. To investigate the method performance a 45 days worth of high resolution (200 ms samples) voltage measurement have been collected and later postprocessed by the proposed method. To further explore the method robustness, the analysis included different method settings and also the influence of different measurement accuracy. To obtain greater certainty of the obtained results, the phase connection of all deployed measuring units has been unified by very accurate signal injection phase identification method. From the obtained results it is found out, that the proposed method can be quite prone to worse performance for cases with lower measurement accuracy with the overall phase identification probability being more than 80 %. To stay in the more robust performance region it is recommended to search for voltage events with higher magnitudes and use longer aggregation intervals (e.g. 10 minutes).

articleTitle: On Verification of Power Generating Modules Compliance with Network Requirements
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The paper deals with operational notification of power generating modules with focus on compliance verification processes with involvement of third-party bodies issuing equipment certificates. The verification processes introduced by EU Commission are analyzed and systematized, and further, their needful and beneficial development has been identified and proposed. In following, means and techniques of the equipment compliance verification (compliance testing, compliance simulation, compliance monitoring) and their respective use cases and limitations are described and upgraded. Finally, timeline for compliance verification process throughout power generating module’s lifetime before and after final operational notification emphasizing deployment of all introduced verification techniques is presented.

articleTitle: Integration of Distributed Energy Generation in Energy Citizen side: Key Barriers and Enablers
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Distributed energy generations (DEGs) form one of the main pillars enabling DER at the citizens and residential premises. Effective deployment of these resources has a key role in the energy transition’s success. Compared to the other energy sector stakeholders, citizens have many specificities that need to be addressed. Analysing and meeting the needs and securing potential engagement in the energy transition is more complicated than dealing with organisations, companies or institutions. This paper thus very specifically analyse the DEG citizen empowerment barriers and main enablers. It examines main challenges and bottlenecks, identifies key enablers, reviews good practices and suggests actions to achieve a smooth and efficient energy transition.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Water Quality Influence on Power Plant Cooling System
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: In the power plants water is widely used in many technological processes. In order to generete electricity is necessery to have constant access to sources of fresh water with its appropriate physical and chemical properties. This work present analysis of parameters in cooling water for maintenance of proper operating parameters of power plant. Cooling water quality can affect power plant performance. In this work water in selected close cooling systems was evaluated for their chemical constituents. Each constituent was analyzed individually to determine possible influence of the maximum allowable concentration on cooling plant perfomrance. Selected water quality parameter was correlated using Pearson coefficient to connect infuence of make-up water to system water parameter. Maintaining water balance, betweent both are the greatest challenges for water in power plant cooling efficiency improvment.

articleTitle: Prospective Direction of Development of Protection Systems for Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) and their development, together with the construction of microgrids, has significantly expanded the interest in such a system, and this change fundamentally alters the traditional concept of central energy production to local production and consumption in microgrids. While the integration of RES causes a reduction in short-circuit ratios due to inverters, they also reduce transmission losses and increase the operational reliability of the distribution network, while at the same time creating new problems that need to be addressed, especially in protection and fault management systems in microgrids. When designing a modern protection system or modifying an existing system to meet new conditions, it is necessary to know as much detail as possible about the local network load as well as the environmental weather effects acting on the resources deployed in such a system. Considerable attention must therefore be paid in the design to all these parameters, which affect both the protection system and the behavior of the network itself. For further research and development of a suitable protection system for microgrids, it is necessary to draw attention to this issue. This paper highlights prospective methods and devices that can be considered in the future development and modification of protection systems for microgrids.

articleTitle: Verification of Characteristics of Selected Current Transformers and Protection Relays
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Protection circuits, specifically current transformers and protection relays, are an important part of electrical networks, enabling safe operation and suppression of dangerous transients and fault conditions. While current transformer requirements and specifications have been standardized for many decades, the aging and wear process of field-installed units has not been a focus of documentation, especially in view of the climate and conditions of Central Europe. In the case of protection relays, works describing the fault recording function are not available, especially with real data. Therefore, this paper presents an experimental evaluation and description of both previously described problems. Measurements are performed per partes; a protection relay tester was used to link the two parts of the evaluation. Due to the intended goal of using the results for estimating the components of the distribution network components and implementing and developing a reliability-centered maintenance strategy, only fault-relevant values (protection cores error ratio, fault recording function) are used. The evaluation is carried out on two oil current transformers (CT) and four protection relays from three manufacturers. The highest current recordings, the evaluation of the error ratio and the values are presented, illustrated and discussed.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Process to Identify the National Smart Grid Research &Innovation Status and Priorities
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper proposes an efficient and dynamic process to evaluate the smart grid research and innovation (R&I) activities in the EU Member States (MS) at the national level where the R&I status of smart grid technologies is identified by analysing the outcomes of completed projects and R&I priorities are extracted from the national energy and climate plan (NECP). Throughout the process, interaction with stakeholders is also very important to identify the R&I needs, verify the outcomes and hence be included in the process. The evaluation outcomes, including the identified technological gaps, can be exploited further to strengthen the action plan of decarbonising the smart grid network at the national level. The proposed process can also be implemented at a regional level to achieve the regional targets. This paper validates the proposed approach by presenting the findings at national and regional levels of three Member States (MS).

articleTitle: Water Quality Control as an Element of Increasing the Operational Safety of Energy Production Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: Water, as well as the fuel, is the primary raw material use in the power generation process. The interdependency between water and energy, sometimes called the water-energy nexus, is growing in importance as demand for both water and energy increases and the increasingly difficult availability of these basic raw materials. Maintaining high quality water is the most important factor in preventing degradation of boilers and cooling towers. It is therefore necessary to be aware of the fact, that ensuring proper water quality is an important element of operational safety of energy production systems. The paper presents the results of research on the quality of water used in the conventional power plant. Constantly monitoring of available resources and possibility to adapt existing treatment systems to the changing quality of the raw water allows to increase the operational safety of energy production systems. The presented research concern both, the quality of water taken from the source and the water used in specific energy production processes. Despite the changes in the quality of water in the source (river), there were no exceedances of the quality parameters in water supplied technological processes, in the investigated period.

articleTitle: DC Arc Flash Calculations in 110V UPS Systems
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: This paper describes the DC arc flash analysis, existing calculation models and arc flash methodology for networks with constant DC voltage sources. For the examined 110V DC UPS system, the main goal was to evaluate DC arc flash conditions and to determine respective PPE categories. The overview of several commercial softwares which currently cover the DC arc flash analysis is also provided.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Flows in a Municipality with High-level PV and EV Penetration
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: The article deals with modeling energy flows at a medium-size municipality with a high roof photovoltaics installation and electric mobility level. The limitations of daily uncontrolled charging are investigated as well as the impact of multi-day charging.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Design Optimization of Highly Efficient Lead-free Perovskite/c-Si Tandem Solar Cell
publicationTitle: 2022 22nd International Scientific Conference on Electric Power Engineering (EPE)
abstract: With the unprecedented development of Perovskite-Si tandem solar cells technology in the last five years, it has become essential to eliminate the toxicity content by using lead-free perovskite materials. For this purpose, a numerical study using the SCAPS-1D simulation tool was demonstrated to investigate lead-free perovskite on the crystalline silicon-based tandem cell structure. The tandem cell combination of (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnIBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), a Pb-free perovskite, as upper absorber layer, and (c-Si) as the lower cell is used for the first time. The suggested tandem structure demonstrates an optimal device efficiency of 30.55%. Our numerical Simulation was done in two steps. First, the top cell CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnIBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and bottom cell (c-Si) are simulated as standalone cells to optimize the performance of these single-junction solar cells. Then, 2-T perovskite/c-Si tandem configuration was performed by utilizing the optimized upper and lower cells. To achieve the current matching point for the two-terminal tandem structure, the upper absorber layer thickness of (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnIBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) should be adjusted to 0.3545 μm. At this thickness, a JSC of 16.08 (mA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) is obtained for the two subcells with efficiencies of 20.58% and 19.22% for the upper and lower cells, respectively. Overall, the CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>SnIBr<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/c-Si tandem cell yields an impressive PCE of 30.55% with VOC of 2.185 V.
